title: Using Set Learning to Improve Set-Valued Classifiers on Long-tailed Data
abstract: arXiv:2610.27443v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Set-valued classification (SVC) offers a practical approach to communicating uncertainty while maintaining accuracy by predicting variable-sized sets per input rather than fixed-sized sets (e.g. top-1 or top-5). However, set-valued classifiers (SVCs) exhibit significantly degraded performance on long-tailed and imbalanced datasets, a setting for which they are ostensibly well-suited. This becomes apparent under macro-average evaluation, which weighs all classes equally. SVCs are typically formed during a post-hoc calibration stage, so little is known about how training dynamics affect their behaviour. In this work, we investigate how different neural network training strategies and loss functions impact downstream SVC performance on highly imbalanced data. translated_title: 利用集合学习改进长尾数据上的集合值分类器
translated_abstract: 集合值分类（SVC）提供了一种在保持准确性的同时传达不确定性的实用方法，它通过为每个输入预测可变大小的集合，而非固定大小的集合（例如 top-1 或 top-5）。然而，集合值分类器在长尾和不平衡数据集上的性能显著下降，而表面上这类场景本应是它们所擅长的。这一问题在宏平均评估下尤为明显，因为宏平均对所有类别赋予相同权重。集合值分类器通常在事后校准阶段形成，因此目前对训练动态如何影响其行为知之甚少。在这项工作中，我们研究了不同的神经网络训练策略和损失函数如何影响高度不平衡数据上的下游集合值分类性能。除了标签平滑和类别平衡等方法外，我们还研究了作用于批次内样本集合（而非逐个处理样本）的损失函数……
tldr: 该论文系统研究了不同训练策略与损失函数（包括作用于批次样本集合的集合式损失）对集合值分类器在长尾不平衡数据上性能的影响，提出通过在训练中引入集合学习来提升其宏平均表现。
en_tdlr: This paper investigates how different training strategies and loss functions—including set-based losses operating over batches of examples—affect set-valued classifiers on highly imbalanced long-tailed data, showing that incorporating set learning during training improves their macro-averaged performance.
